notes.meaning: Jesus had finished all his public teaching and now spoke plainly about his coming death. The Passover was a yearly feast remembering how God rescued Israel from Egypt, and Jesus showed he would be sacrificed as the true Passover Lamb. He knew the exact time he would be handed over to die on a cross, showing he was giving his life willingly.

The Jewish ruling council, made up of chief priests and community leaders, met at the palace of Caiaphas the high priest. They were deeply threatened by Jesus and plotted a secret way to arrest him and have him killed. Their wicked plan fulfilled ancient prophecy about rulers plotting against the Lord's anointed King.

The leaders wanted to avoid arresting Jesus during the week of the festival because huge crowds filled Jerusalem and loved him. They feared a riot would break out if they attacked him openly. Yet God overruled their timing so that Jesus died on the feast day as the true sacrifice.

While Jesus was eating in the village of Bethany at the home of Simon, who had likely been cured of leprosy, a woman brought a very costly white stone jar of fragrant perfume. She broke it and poured the rich oil over his head to show deep love and honor to him as God's King. This generous act was a supreme sign of devotion and faith.

The disciples became angry at this act and called it a wasteful loss. Led by Judas, they argued that the expensive perfume could have been sold for nearly a whole year of wages to help poor people. They failed to understand the special honor due to Jesus and masked cold hearts behind a holy excuse.

Jesus immediately came to the woman's defense and told the disciples to stop troubling her. He called her deed a noble and beautiful act done directly for him. God is pleased when our heartfelt love is poured out on his Son, even if others criticize it.

Jesus explained that the disciples would always have needy people nearby to care for, but his bodily presence on earth was coming to a quick end. Caring for the poor is a constant Christian duty, but this was a unique, fleeting moment to honor the Lord before his death. Special acts of devotion to Christ must not be judged as neglect of charity.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christ is not always present in a visible, earthly manner, but he remains truly present with the church in the mystery of the Eucharist.

notes.meaning: Jesus explained the true meaning of the woman's action, showing that she had anointed his body beforehand for burial. In those days, bodies were lovingly anointed with sweet spices before being placed in a tomb. Because his coming resurrection would leave no time for this afterward, her gift was God's way of preparing him for the grave.

Jesus promised that wherever the good news of salvation is told across the world, this woman's deed would be remembered. While worldly rulers are quickly forgotten, genuine love for Christ earns lasting honor in God's story. This prophecy has come true as her loving act continues to be read and admired in every land.

Judas Iscariot, one of Jesus' twelve chosen apostles, went straight to the chief priests to sell his Master. He agreed to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver, which was the legal price of a common slave. His greed led him to treat the Lord of glory as a cheap item to trade away.

From that moment on, Judas watched for a quiet chance to deliver Jesus into the hands of the priests. He looked for a time when Jesus was away from the crowds so there would be no public rescue. A heart gripped by the love of money will steadily plan and carry out terrible evil.

On the day the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed and unleavened bread prepared, the disciples asked Jesus where he wanted them to set up the holy meal. Jesus had no house of his own in the city, having become poor for our sake. Even while his enemies plotted his death, Jesus faithfully kept God's law.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note a calendar puzzle between the Gospels, suggesting that Jesus may have eaten the Passover meal one day early because he knew he would already be dead by the regular hour.

notes.meaning: Jesus sent his disciples to an unnamed friend in the city with a message that his appointed time of suffering was near. By keeping the location secret until the last moment, Jesus prevented Judas from having him arrested before the meal could be shared. The disciples obeyed their Master's instructions, found everything as he said, and readied the lamb and bitter herbs.

When evening arrived, Jesus lay back around the table on dining couches with his twelve disciples to eat the Passover meal. While they were eating, Jesus startled them with a solemn announcement that one of his own closest companions would betray him. His words showed his complete knowledge of all that was about to happen.

The disciples were filled with deep sorrow and began asking Jesus one by one if he meant them. They did not immediately suspect Judas or blame each other, but looked honestly into their own weak hearts with godly fear. True followers of Christ distrust their own strength and want their Lord to search their minds.

Jesus replied that the traitor was one who was dipping bread into the common bowl of sauce with him. Sharing food from the same dish was an ancient sign of close friendship and trust, making this betrayal far more painful and evil. This fulfilled the Old Testament psalm about a trusted friend lifting up his heel against God's servant.

Jesus declared that he must die on the cross exactly as God had planned and recorded in the Scriptures, but that did not excuse the man who betrayed him. God's sovereign control over history never removes human guilt for willful sin. Jesus pronounced a terrible curse on the traitor, warning that it would have been better for that person never to have been born.

Judas spoke up last, asking with bold hypocrisy if he was the one, calling Jesus only 'Teacher' instead of 'Lord.' Jesus quietly answered that Judas had spoken the truth, exposing the secret treachery in his heart. Even when warned to his face, Judas remained hardened and refused to repent.
